reportDialog.title: Share an emergency
reportDialog.description1: We are based in Lviv, but please remember - we are not a shelter and do not have our own facilities for long-term animal care. We primarily recommend reaching out to:
reportDialog.description4: There are similar organizations in other cities that can provide assistance.
reportDialog.description: Choose a convenient way to contact us, describe the problem, and we'll route it to the right volunteer as soon as possible.

paragraphs.intro1: We know that not everyone can rescue, treat, or rehome animals alone, so the foundation supports people who refuse to stay indifferent.
paragraphs.intro2: You are not left alone with a difficult situation. Your effort becomes part of a larger rescue system, letting you change an animal’s destiny without spending every resource on your own.
paragraphs.cta: From our side you can receive:

medical.title: Medical guidance and treatment support
medical.description: We help you find veterinarians and co-fund treatment or sterilization for stray animals.

adoption.title: Rehoming support
adoption.description: We publish information about rescued animals on our platforms and help them find temporary or permanent homes.

volunteers.title: Volunteer care
volunteers.description: We provide food, carriers, medications, and essentials to people who temporarily shelter an animal.

education.title: Sharing knowledge
education.description: We teach how to act safely and effectively when you find a stray animal.

receive.title: Join the support network
receive.intro: Any help is tangible and important. The more people step in, the lighter the load for everyone—that is exactly the approach we want to build.
receive.callout: We need active participants for different directions:

paragraphs.p1: Trips to assigned locations help us search for and monitor stray animals, assess their health, count individuals, and record conditions like shelter, food access, and interaction with people or other animals.
paragraphs.p2: Every visit ends with a short report describing health status, location specifics, potential risks (for example hostile people or unsafe areas), and recommendations such as urgent veterinary help or sterilization.

paragraphs.p1: We capture stray animals for sterilization, treatment, or relocation, respond to emergencies where animals need immediate help, and evaluate every scene to choose the next steps.
paragraphs.p2: Volunteers transport animals to safe places, clinics, or shelters using nets, carriers, or other tools; experience with animals (clinics, shelters, volunteer programs) is a plus.
paragraphs.p3: Detailed documentation is crucial: the location, animal condition, capture circumstances, and next actions, such as transferring the case to veterinary services.

paragraphs.p1: Volunteers perform medical examinations, assess health, and carry out procedures such as vaccination, sterilization, or treatment both in equipped rooms and directly in the field.
paragraphs.p2: They handle wound care, administer medicines, or perform surgeries; in the field they stabilize animals, provide first aid, and help organize transport to a safe place or clinic.
paragraphs.p3: Accurate records about each animal, procedures, medicines, and follow-up recommendations are required in either digital or paper form.

it.title: IT field

paragraphs.p1: We are building a convenient platform for visitors and volunteers—personal dashboards, interactive stray-location maps, and trip-planning tools.

it.rolesIntro: To keep the process efficient we welcome specialists in different roles:

designers.label: designers
designers.description: to craft inviting and accessible interfaces

analysts.label: business analysts
analysts.description: to capture user needs and prioritize features

paragraphs.p1: The foundation does not have a large shelter, so temporary housing for adult or young stray pets during quarantine or treatment is incredibly valuable.
paragraphs.p2: A covered, safe area—or an adapted wing of a home or commercial space—dramatically accelerates assistance. Several small safe houses across the city are easier to support than transporting every animal to one distant site. Safety and comfort for people and animals remain the main criteria.
paragraphs.p3: We provide food, bedding, litter boxes, and other supplies. Volunteers record health updates, procedures, medicines, and care recommendations in whichever format is convenient.
paragraphs.p4: Ideas on how to organize such spaces, even without your own premises, are also a meaningful contribution.

receive.closing: We appreciate every level of involvement—from one-time help to regular participation—and we will always respect your experience and comfort when selecting tasks.
receive.contactCta: Send us a message and let’s get acquainted ❤️

contactspage.title: Contact
contactspage.aboutus: We're a small, passionate team dedicated to animal welfare. While we don't have a physical shelter, we partner with veterinary clinics to provide treatment and temporary housing for animals in need as they wait for their forever homes.
contactspage.map1: We primarily operate within the zone shown on the map. While our reach is focused, we strive to be helpful for as many animals as possible within our operational capacity.
contactspage.map2: We strive to expand our influence on helping stray animals over a larger zone. This requires the participation of more people, and we invite everyone to join the team.
contactspage.section2_intro: Write your thoughts and we will try to take them into account in our work.

historypage.title: History of our animals
historypage.panel1: We register animals that we monitor, care for, and treat. Each history is our inspiration and helps coordinate the efforts of volunteers and clinics to provide the best care. Each record has a unique story, characteristics, and conditions.

mission.title: Our mission: Control & Response
mission.description: Every surgery prevents dozens of kittens from harsh street life. Our goal is to reduce animal suffering and improve their quality of life.

population.title: Population control
population.description: Humane sterilization is the most effective long-term solution for stray animals.

medical.title: Medical assistance
medical.description: We secure vaccines and trauma treatment for stray cats.

community.title: Community support
community.description: We train and equip neighbors so they can protect local colonies.

1.title: Observation
1.description: We begin with careful street monitoring to understand colony size and members.

2.title: Identification
2.description: The team checks ear clips and tags to see which cats are already sterilized and who still needs help.

3.title: Capture
3.description: We use humane traps and a lot of patience so the process stays calm and safe.

4.title: Veterinary visit
4.description: Each animal sees a licensed vet for diagnostics, and vaccinations.

5.title: Treatment & sterilization
5.description: The core step that prevents uncontrolled reproduction and heals injuries or parasites.

6.title: Rehabilitation
6.description: Animals recover in specialized facilities with care until they are healthy.

7.title: Return or adoption
7.description: Wild animals return to their territory. Socialized animals seek loving homes through publications.
